key_insight: Apparent advantages of real connectome wiring can reverse when model physiology is constrained by independent data rather than tuned for performance.
engineering_relevance: For computational model validation, structural comparisons need matched optimisation and independently constrained parameters to distinguish genuine structural effects from calibration bias.
method: Compare real-wiring physiology transferred to nulls (P1), separately tuned wiring models (P2), and data-constrained tuning (P3).
Test biological conclusions using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.
Check robustness with held-out runs and extended retraining.
evidence_signal: In the mushroom-body model, real wiring beat a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but lost by 0.09 under P3; 95% confidence intervals excluded zero, and held-out runs confirmed the reversal.
watch_item: Failure under data-consistent physiology may reveal model inadequacy rather than inferior biological wiring; some flyvis rankings also depended on the retraining checkpoint.
paper_title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
